title: Cryobank Operations (Awareness Level)
desc: Understand how biological sample banks are run: consent, labelling, cold storage, records, security and ethics. Awareness only.
outcomes: Explain what a cryobank stores and why consent matters.
Fill a sample record and label correctly.
Find risks in the cold chain.
Judge a bank's policies for security and fairness.
task: Create a daily operations checklist and a sample record template for a practice cryobank, and run a mock audit.
condition: A computer, practice forms and a mentor. No real samples, personal data or hazardous materials are used.
standard: Checklist covers temperature, alarms, labelling, access and records; mock audit finds at least 3 planted errors; peers rate Meets or better.
who: Lab trainees, hospital store staff, health administrators.
evidence: checklist, record template, mock audit report
modules: Banks store cells, tissue or cord blood at very low temperatures.
Used for later treatment or research under consent.
Each sample has an owner and conditions of use.
A family stores cord blood; a contract states how long and who can request it.
Summary names consent, storage and use.
People must know what they agree to.
Consent in plain language; the right to withdraw.
Rules for research use and disposal.
Children's samples need guardian consent and review at adulthood in many places.
A form has a tick box for research use that defaults to No.
A sample without a correct label is lost.
Unique ID, date, type, volume, location.
Two-person check at entry and removal.
ID C-2031 is logged in tank 2, rack B, box 4, slot 7.
Daily log of temperature and nitrogen or power levels.
Alarms with call-out lists; backup power.
A night alarm leads to a refill within 20 minutes.
Mark risks on a floor plan.
Extreme cold and gases are hazards.
Oxygen sensors in rooms with nitrogen.
Staff leave the room immediately when the oxygen alarm sounds.
Badge access, camera at doors, visitor log.
Only authorised staff see identity data.
Data is stored securely and deleted per rule.
Staff must show a badge and sign the log for each entry.
No misleading claims about future cures.
Exit plan if a bank closes.
A bank has a written plan to transfer samples if it closes.
The audit finds a missing second-person check and a late log.
quiz: Cells, tissue or cord blood at low temperatures.
Use, duration, research, right to withdraw.
Steps to move samples if the bank closes.
Records showing who did what and when.
To show control and find faults.
rubric: Every claim linked to a dated record and checked by a peer
Checked, dated and explained to others
next: stem cells awareness, DNA analysis, privacy protection practice.
local: Laws for storing human tissue and data differ by place.
ladder: L1: learner can say what a cryobank stores.
L3: learner can fill a record correctly.
L4: learner can run daily checks.
L5: learner can audit a bank.
L6: learner can lead a small shift.
L7: learner can advise on policy.
